## Natural history notes

A medium-sized flycatcher characterized by a gray throat and breast, bright yellow belly, brownish upperparts, rufous highlights in the wings and tail, and a loud rolling call from the canopy. In Florida, the Great Crested Flycatcher is found in hardwood hammocks, pine woods, forest edges, wooded parks, swamps, yards, and mature trees with natural cavities or nest boxes. It feeds mainly on flying insects and other arthropods captured from exposed perches, but also eats berries and small fruits, and nests in tree cavities often lined with bark, leaves, feathers, and shed snakeskin.
